rows.text: Fifty-five lands. That is not a typo and it is not greed — in this deck lands ARE the spells. Windgrace's plus turns the flood into cards, his minus rebuilds whatever you spent, and half the card pool sacrifices its own lands on purpose because a land hitting your graveyard is a trigger, not a loss. The deck is a value engine that happens to look like a mana base.

rows.name: Lord Windgrace
rows.text: the +2 discards and draws, and draws an EXTRA card if what you pitched was a land — so every excess land in hand is a two-for-one. The -3 returns two lands from the graveyard to the battlefield, which is two landfall triggers as well as two lands. The ultimate destroys six nonland permanents and leaves six forestwalking 2/2s, which usually just ends the game.
Play him early and plus him every turn. He is not a bomb you save; he is a draw engine that also protects itself by making Cat tokens on the way out.

guide.title: Lands as a resource, not a cost

rows.name: Constant Mists
rows.text: buyback for a land. A fog every single turn, forever, and every buyback feeds Titania.

rows.name: Crop Rotation
rows.text: one mana, sacrifice a land, fetch ANY land onto the battlefield. It finds Cabal Coffers, Field of the Dead or a missing colour at instant speed.

rows.name: Harrow

rows.name: Roiling Regrowth
rows.text: the same effect on a slower body.

rows.name: Scapeshift
rows.text: sacrifice as many lands as you like and replace them all. With Titania out it is a board of 5/3s; with Field of the Dead it is a board of Zombies.

rows.name: The Gitrog Monster
rows.text: an extra land drop, deathtouch on a 6/6, and a card for EVERY land that reaches your graveyard. Its upkeep sacrifice is not a drawback here — it is a free draw.

rows.name: Splendid Reclamation
rows.text: returns every land from your graveyard to the battlefield at once. After a Scapeshift or a few turns of sacrificing, this is ten or more landfall triggers in one card.

rows.name: Life from the Loam
rows.text: three lands back to hand, and dredge means it recurs itself every turn.

rows.name: Crucible of Worlds
rows.text: play lands from the graveyard. It turns every sacrifice effect above into a repeatable engine.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep lands and one engine piece. A hand of six lands and Exploration is a fine keep here — this is one of the very few decks where flooding is the plan rather than the failure case.
Windgrace's +2 is not a last resort. Use it every turn you have a spare land in hand, even when you do not need cards; two-for-ones compound faster than any single spell in the deck.

rows.name: Crucible of Worlds
rows.text: prioritise it. Every land-sacrifice effect in the deck goes from one-shot to repeatable the turn it lands.

rows.name: Titania, Protector of Argoth
rows.text: hold Constant Mists until she is out if you can afford to. Fogging with Titania on the battlefield turns a defensive card into a 5/3 a turn.
